contexts: about 35 alerts a week, four percent real
six duty epidemiologists, no written procedure
reading: The checklist acts on the epidemiologist's process, not on the signal, so its value lies in faster and more consistent decisions without more dismissed true events. An accuracy framing needs a reference standard that hindsight corrupts. A randomised comparison of procedures measures time directly, but contamination between arms is likely when the same people validate both, which day-level randomisation addresses. True events are rare, so missed events need case-by-case review rather than a test.
